status: partial sequential obstruction independently reviewed PASS; all four P02 atoms unresolved

report.report:
The stated partial theorem is established, including the additional approximation claims in the manuscript. This verdict does not resolve any full catalogue atom.

The geometry and field hypotheses are correct. K=k((pi)) is complete and nontrivially discretely valued in every characteristic. The displayed Tate spectra are good and strict. Their diagonals are closed immersions, giving separatedness; Tate-algebra dimension theory gives pure dimensions one and n. No algebraic closedness of K is required.

Step 1 is valid. Reduction proves multiplicativity of the Gauss norm, and every bounded multiplicative seminorm is dominated by that norm. Consequently eta is the unique Shilov boundary point of D. The singleton is closed, so w is upper semicontinuous, and its restriction to Int(D) is zero. The retrieved boundary-extension theorem has precisely the scalar-extension meaning required here. Curve subharmonicity therefore establishes classical psh, and analytic pullback establishes the claim for u. The boundary composition formula is used with its equality hypothesis satisfied by the separated structural morphism of D. Its reverse inclusion then puts p^{-1}(eta), including x, in the relative boundary. These statements were checked against [GR v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13548v2).

Steps 2–3 establish the stronger obstruction to arbitrary continuous sequences. A normalized restricted series has nonzero polynomial reduction, with finitely many coefficient roots. Outside those roots its evaluation agrees exactly with its Gauss evaluation. Finite evaluation conditions therefore exclude only finitely many coefficient points from any neighborhood of eta. Countably many continuity neighborhoods exclude at most countably many such points. Choosing a remaining a gives |h_j(i(a))−h_j(x)|<1/4 for every j, incompatible with the respective limits 0 and 1. The argument also works when each term is continuous only on its individual neighborhood of x. For logarithmic maxima allowing a base locus, decreasing convergence implies each term is at least 1 at x, so some analytic section is nonzero there; this supplies the required local continuity. All four sequential conclusions follow.

Step 4 is correct. Discreteness gives ||f−q||≤|pi|<1 after normalization and coefficient-field lifting. Thus |f(y)|<1 implies |q(y)|<1. Factoring the nonzero polynomial q over k forces |T−a|(y)<1 for some a. The constant-polynomial case is correctly excluded. This argument requires algebraic closedness only of the coefficient field.

Step 5 gives globally defined approximants on the fixed spaces. The identity v_{F,m}=log max(1,|pi^{-1}P_F^m|) verifies the prescribed basepoint-free Fubini–Study convention. The two strict Laurent domains give integral PL expressions, agreeing on their overlap. Logarithmic psh and finite-max stability establish classical psh; the good, strict, nontrivially valued hypotheses needed for semipositivity are satisfied. Since every factor has norm at most one, both index coordinates decrease the function. For a detected point with r=|T−a|(y)<1, every sufficiently large index containing a has v_{F,m}(y)=0. At eta every term equals 1. This proves decreasing pointwise convergence, including the empty-F and zero-factor cases.

Step 6 also checks out. The convolution has lambda′≥0, lambda″(t)=rho(−t)≥0, and the stated constant and linear tails. On the unit locus, with t=−log|P_F|, the Hessian of g(t)=lambda(1−mt) is m²rho(mt−1)≥0. Ordinary moment-map calculus therefore gives an ordinary CLD-smooth function with positive smooth Hessian. Near every zero of P_F the function is identically zero, providing compatible ordinary-open expressions there. Positivity at relative boundary points is smooth-form positivity; the usual Hessian-current tests apply on the relative interior. The same expressions work after every analytic field extension. Their limit upstairs is exactly the pullback of u, without identifying its support with a single upstairs Gauss point. The relevant positivity convention is supported by [CLD v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2).

Step 7 establishes the precise countability claim. For countable k, the increasing initial segments F_j together with m_j=j form a cofinal sequence. For uncountable k, countably many finite subsets cannot be cofinal. Neither displayed net converges locally uniformly at x, since its limit is discontinuous there.

One harmless comparison correction is required: [GJR Proposition 15.11](https://smf.emath.fr/system/files/filepdf/GUBLER_JELL_RABINOFF.pdf) treats arbitrary Thuillier-subharmonic functions on smooth boundaryless curves and produces a decreasing net. It requires neither continuity nor a proper algebraic curve. The manuscript conflates that result with a different continuous current-psh curve case. The example remains outside the GJR case because of its relative boundary, so this correction changes no proof or conclusion. The continuous invariant toric cases in the supplied dossier likewise do not apply to this discontinuous starting function.

No novelty or priority claim is made or established. The arithmetic check and compilation are correctly described as nonproof evidence; this verdict does not certify the archival hashes or build artifacts.

passages.statement: For an affinoid algebra A over a complete non-Archimedean field, M(A) is compact Hausdorff in the topology generated by analytic evaluations and has a finite unique minimal Shilov boundary.
For an affinoid analytic curve over a complete non-Archimedean field, meaning a separated analytic space of pure dimension one, its relative boundary equals its Shilov boundary.

For a separated pure one-dimensional analytic space C over a complete non-Archimedean field, every upper semicontinuous v:C→R∪{−∞} subharmonic on Int(C) is subharmonic on C under GR Definition 3.4, which tests all nontrivially valued analytic extensions and morphisms from smooth connected strict curves.

For analytic spaces over complete non-Archimedean fields, classical psh is preserved by analytic morphisms and is preserved and reflected by analytic field extension; on separated pure one-dimensional analytic spaces it equals subharmonicity.

For analytic spaces over complete non-Archimedean fields, classical psh is preserved by analytic morphisms and is preserved and reflected by analytic field extension; on separated pure one-dimensional analytic spaces it equals subharmonicity.

On an analytic space over a complete non-Archimedean field, log|f| is classically psh for every analytic f; nonnegative linear combinations and finite maxima of classically psh functions are classically psh.
Over a complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field, a real-valued real-PL function on a good strictly analytic space is semipositive if and only if it is classically psh (GR v2, Theorem 4.3).
For analytic morphisms X→Y→S over a complete non-Archimedean field, ∂(X/S)⊆∂(X/Y)∪f^{-1}(∂(Y/S)), with equality if Y→S is locally separated.
For a complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field F and integer n≥1, F<T_1,…,T_n> is an integral regular Tate algebra of Krull dimension n.
For a complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field F and integer n≥1, F<T_1,…,T_n> is an integral regular Tate algebra of Krull dimension n.
For a complete non-Archimedean field F and an integral strictly F-affinoid algebra A, M(A) has pure analytic dimension dim_Krull(A).
For a complete non-Archimedean field F and an integral strictly F-affinoid algebra A, M(A) has pure analytic dimension dim_Krull(A).

On good separated pure-dimensional analytic spaces over a complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field, smooth convex Euclidean functions pulled back through ordinary analytic moment-map tropicalizations are ordinary CLD-smooth with positive d′d″, hence psh; this smooth-form assertion includes relative boundary points.
passages.quote: Une fonction tropicalement convexe est psh.

passages.statement: On good strictly analytic spaces over a complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field, real-PL functions and weakly smooth functions are continuous real-valued functions.
On good strictly analytic spaces over a complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field, real-PL functions and weakly smooth functions are continuous real-valued functions.

Let F be a complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field, C a smooth separated F-analytic curve of pure dimension one, where smooth means rig-smooth and boundaryless, and f a Thuillier-subharmonic function on C. For every relatively compact ordinary open U⊂C, a decreasing net of weakly smooth psh functions on U converges pointwise to f|U (GJR, Proposition 15.11).

post_review_edits: Corrected the GJR curve comparison to arbitrary Thuillier-subharmonic functions and decreasing nets on smooth boundaryless curves
Updated verification metadata; theorem and proof unchanged
reviewed_scope: On strict closed polydiscs over K=k((pi)) with uncountable algebraically closed k, a bounded classical psh boundary-jump function has no local pointwise continuous approximating sequence at the specified boundary point; explicit decreasing Fubini–Study/real-PL and ordinary smooth psh nets still converge. This separates nets from sequences, not general regularization or boundaryless spaces.
